verdict.rationale: LangGraph's core Graph API models agent workflows as explicit graphs of State, Nodes and Edges, and states that composing them creates "complex, looping workflows". Its multi-agent docs let you embed other patterns as nodes in a custom workflow, and community users confirm its Pregel/BSP design supports cycles and parallelism. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of conditional branching and of parallel fan-out (parallelism is evidenced only by community reports).

support.subject: As a developer, I can compose agents into an explicit graph or workflow with branching, loops, and parallel steps

citations.quote: LangGraph models agent workflows as graphs. You define the behavior of your agents using three key components: State, Nodes, Edges.
By composing Nodes and Edges, you can create complex, looping workflows that evolve the state over time.
Embed other patterns as nodes in your workflow.
It's a Pregel/BSP-based orchestration for cycles and parallelism without data races; can design your graph as a state machine.
